Traders reported that spot premium quotations for imported cathode have been volatile in the last two weeks. The latest quotation for imported cathode is $50-90/t, with only a few deals being closed at $7080/t. The premium for imported EW cathode is $5070/t. The SHFE/LME cash price ratio has declined to around 7.5 in the past two weeks, which is the lowest so far in 2010. However, the current ‘strong LME and weak SHFE' situation does not imply weak domestic demand. We believe that with the surge in the LME copper price, domestic consumers are hesitant to buy. The imported cathode market is subdued except for some activity by traders. We believe that demand may see only a modest seasonal improvement in Q4, following a stronger than usual Q3. Moreover, high copper prices may constrain buying interest in the short term. In addition, RMB appreciation may accelerate the 'strong LME and weak SHFE' trend. Some large traders maintain a high premium quotation. It is reasonable that they are trying to minimize their losses given the current negative price difference between SHFE and LME, and in addition the annual premium negotiation season is approaching. Traders suggest that the loss on importing cathode has risen to around RMB 3,000/t right now. We believe a high copper price and bullish market sentiment before annual premium negotiations may cause the spot premium quotation to become more volatile in the near future. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 1 of 3 **October 2010** www.crumonitor.com With respect to the annual premium negotiations, until now we have heard figures in the $100-115/t range suggested. # **China raises six banks' deposit reserve ratio** The China Central Bank notified BOC, ICBC, CCB and ABC, the four state-owned banks, as well as MINSHENG and CMB, which are joint-equity banks, that they had to increase the deposit reserve ratio by 50 basis points on 11th October. The deposit ratio for BOC, ICBC, CCB and ABC will reach 17.5% and for MINSHENG and CMB the figure is 15.5%. It is the third time that the China Central Bank has raised required reserves in 2010, with the four state owned banks deposit reserve ratio surging to an all time high. Market participants understand the adjustment will be effective in reducing the excess liquidity in the market. New loans in September continued to increase and a lot of central bank bills are due to be paid off. The fact that foreign exchange holdings in both August and September were inc

reasing, shows that liquidity may be too abundant in the short term. Moreover, raising required reserves may be needed to control inflation expectations. In addition, some control on capital inflows into the market may help to cool the real estate market. Obviously, the deposit reserve ratio increase is negative for the copper price because it reduces liquidity in the market. However, the recent market sentiment is bullish, with a weak US dollar and improved fundamentals continuing to support copper price. It seems that market insiders ignore this negative news. Furthermore, some market participants believe that the required reserve has already been close to a historical high. There is limited scope for further increases in the near future. # **How Chinese copper consumption may respond to a surging price in Q4?** After the LME 3-month copper price broke through $8,000/t, it continued to rise in the following two weeks, supported by the weak US dollar and prospects of renewed monetary stimulus in US. We believe that the fundamentals are also crucial for determining whether the copper price will continue to rise from the current high level, in particular the response of Chinese copper consumption to the surging price. We heard reports from some copper wirerod producers that they are consuming their raw material and semis products inventory now. The high copper price may constrain end users buying enthusiasm. Moreover, along with the copper price rising, more scrap is available in the market and the discount between scrap and cathode has widened. Copper wirerod producers who use scrap as raw materials may increase as opposed to producers who use cathode. Copper tube is currently the strongest copper semis sector in China, benefiting from home appliance stimulus package. However, copper tube producers’ operating rates have been declining due to seasonal factors. Usually, November to May is the strong season for Chinese copper tube producers. In addition, they feel a negative impact from tightened credit. The current market situation may bring more uncertainty to the strong season in November and December. For copper plate, sheet and strip manufacturers, after July and August weak season consumption has improved in September, with capacity utilization up 2.6% m-o-m. However they have become more cautious now. Some of them estimate that consumption improvement in Q4 may be limited. Furthermore Chinese energy conservation continues to affect copper semis production in Zhejiang and Jiangsu province currently. During LME week we felt that almost everyone was bullish for copper. LME 3-month copper price continues to surge and as of Friday 15th it hit $8400/t, a 27-month high. Apart from strong investment enthusiasm, market players have some concerns. Producers may worry about demand destruction and competitive materials’ long term substitution for copper such as aluminum, whereas final consumers may suffer from the high copper price. We believe that the copper price may become more volatile and maintain high levels in the short term. SHFE 3- month copper price rose to RMB63,890/t this Friday which is the highest price since July 2008. The Shanghai physical market is subdued with RMB130/t average spot discount. We believe that with the SHFE delivery day approaching, physical discounts may widen next week. We understand that domestic supply of refined copper is abundant right now. SHFE cathode inventory was up 16,063t to103,510t, compared to two weeks ago. Moreover more scrap is available in the spot market due to the high copper price. According to the preliminary Chinese custom data China import 410,000t of scrap in September up 5.2% m-o-m. We heard reports that some smelters do not even have enough space to put the scrap. Despite this, any demand improvement in Q4 is constrained by surging copper price.
